patterns.label: Qal
patterns.explain: Qal is the simple, basic stem, usually active.

patterns.label: Niphal
patterns.explain: Niphal is the stem that is usually passive, reflexive or middle.

patterns.label: Piel
patterns.explain: Piel is the intensive stem, with a doubled middle consonant.

patterns.label: Pual
patterns.explain: Pual is the passive of Piel.

patterns.label: Hiphil
patterns.explain: Hiphil is the causative stem, with a prefixed ה.

patterns.label: Hophal
patterns.explain: Hophal is the passive of Hiphil.

patterns.label: Hithpael
patterns.explain: Hithpael is the reflexive or reciprocal stem, with a prefixed הִת.

types.label: Strong Verb
types.explain: A strong verb has no weak consonant in its root (no guttural, no א, נ, י or ו in a weak position, no final ה, and no doubled root consonant).

types.label: I-Guttural
types.explain: The first root consonant is a guttural (ה, ח or ע).

types.label: I-Aleph
types.explain: The first root consonant is א.

types.label: I-Nun
types.explain: The first root consonant is נ, which often assimilates into the next consonant (this includes לקח).

types.label: I-Vav / I-Yod
types.explain: The first root consonant is a vav or a yod (written י in the lexicon).

types.label: II-Guttural
types.explain: The second root consonant is a guttural (א, ה, ח, ע or ר).

types.label: II-Vav / II-Yod (Hollow)
types.explain: The second root consonant is a vav or a yod, and the root is “hollow”: the middle consonant is a vowel in many forms.

types.label: II-Geminate
types.explain: The second and third root consonants are the same.

types.label: III-Guttural
types.explain: The third root consonant is ח or ע.

types.label: III-Aleph
types.explain: The third root consonant is א.

types.label: III-He
types.explain: The third root consonant is ה.
